title: Comparative Phytochemical Studies of Callus Regenerated from Leaf Explant of Prunus africana (Hook. f.) Kalkman and Stem Bark of the Same Mother Plant
content: The overexploitation of the endangered medicinal tree Prunus africana (Hook. f.) Kalkman for its stem bark calls for alternative sources of therapeutic metabolites. This study compared the phytochemical composition of callus regenerated from leaf explants with that of the stem bark of the same mother plant. Leaf explants were cultured on Murashige and Skoog medium and sub-cultured every 30 days for 120 days. Dried callus and stem bark were extracted with 70% ethanol and water and analysed by qualitative phytochemical screening, thin-layer chromatography (TLC) and high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) fingerprinting. Callus weight increased exponentially up to 90 days before plateauing, and callus extracts gave higher extraction yields than stem bark extracts. Both tissues contained steroids, alkaloids, anthraquinones, phenolics and terpenoids and shared diagnostic TLC bands and HPLC peaks (4.2, 8.0 and 10.7 min), although peak intensities and some minor signals differed. Flavonoids were not detected in either tissue. Leaf explant callus culture therefore retains the characteristic phytochemical profile of P. africana stem bark and offers a non-destructive, scalable route to standardised botanical metabolites that supports the conservation of this endangered species.
